event: Weekly Market Review
title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Tech cracked; hard assets and defensives absorbed the week's risk.

The Dow's 0.95% decline badly understates the damage: QQQ fell 4.98% while gold gained 4.71%, a divergence of nearly 10 points. The week began with a tech-led rout and ended Friday with dip buyers lifting QQQ 1.40% off the low. On Friday, November 6, a hot jobs print (nonfarm payrolls 16.5 vs. 6.5 forecast) initially reinforced the inflation trade but the tape finished buying growth back. The rotation, not the direction, is the story.

INDICES — QQQ -4.98% worst of the major indices; SPY -2.70%; IWM -2.03%; DIA -0.95% held best. Small beat large by 0.81pp (IJR -1.89%), and QQQ is now below its 200-day MA. VIX closed at 25.6, nearly a full point above its 20-day average of 18.8, with QQQ ATM IV at 32.2%. The standout cross-asset move was SLV +5.09% and GLD +4.71%, while DIA was the only major index to avoid a >2% weekly loss.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLC Communication Services +4.89%; XLRE Real Estate +1.92%; XLY Consumer Discretionary +1.91%; XLF Financials +1.15%; XLP Consumer Staples +0.74%; XLV Health Care -0.04%; XLU Utilities -0.69%; XLB Materials -1.50%; XLI Industrials -2.83%; XLK Technology -8.23%; XLE Energy -12.00%. The top two industries were GDX +13.63% and TAN +13.38%, while the bottom two were XOP -14.72% and DRAM -18.16%. The money flow shows a clear rotation: $977mm into XLV (98th percentile) and $816mm into XLF (90th percentile) versus $710mm out of XLC. Energy collapsed on both the price and industry level, with XLE -12.00% leading the decline and XOP -14.72% behind it. Rotation-state label: defensive risk-off, with real assets and health care absorbing the outflows, though XLK's $491mm inflow suggests the selling wasn't wholesale.

DRIVERS — The dominant driver was the unwind of technology exposure: XLK fell 8.23% and SOXX -71.04% led the decline, while the long-duration real-asset complex (SLV +5.09%, GDX +13.63%) acted as a haven. Friday's jobs report beat expectations (nonfarm 16.5 vs. 6.5; unemployment 4.1% vs. 4.2% forecast) alongside Michigan consumer sentiment at 51 vs. 48, which initially pushed risk off but the tape recovered into the close with a 1.40% move in QQQ. Volatility elevated sharply, with VIX at 25.6 vs. 18.8 on a 20-day basis, and SPY ATM IV at 21.2%, signaling real demand for hedges. The dollar firmed (UUP +0.73%) while gold and silver rose anyway, a notable divergence that could reflect positioning rather than fresh fundamentals. Breadth was weak, with 179 advancers to 322 decliners, though the tape is not in a state of absolute panic.

WHAT'S NEXT — Watch whether XLK and SOXX bounce digs deeper or turns into a base; QQQ's 32.2% implied vol suggests the market expects large moves either way. The tech tape's 20-day decline is already in place, so positioning toward the next leg could be an opportunity if the bounce holds. Keep an eye on breadth improving, since 55% above the 200-day MA leaves room for more sustained participation. The energy weakness in XLE and XOP may be worth watching for a contrarian setup if it becomes exhausted.
